comparison: Strong agreement on MER21C insertion in Euarchontoglires and sequence conservation. Both evaluations affirm the phylogenetic and comparative genomic evidence (C17-C21, C56-C66, C104-C105, C129-C132). Reviewers explicitly praised the genomic analysis and evidence for functional conservation of the MER21C relic in rodents.

Strong agreement on correlation between MER21C presence and ZDBF2 imprinting. Both evaluations support claims C51-C55, C91, C96 regarding allele-specific expression and germline DMRs. Reviewers explicitly confirmed imprinting demonstration in rabbit and rhesus macaque, with editor noting 'evidence is now convincing.'

Strong agreement on RNA-seq methodology and GPR1-AS detection requirements. Both evaluations support claims C44-C49, C122-C125 regarding directional RNA-seq depth requirements and species distribution. Reviewers praised the generation of high-quality RNA-seq data from diverse species.

Agreement on mouse MER21C relic promoter activity (C67-C68). OpenEval covers broader claims including transcription factor binding sites (C69-C72), while peer review focuses on experimental validation of promoter activity via luciferase assays, which was added in revision to address reviewer concerns.

Partial overlap on transcription factor binding sites and temporal expression. OpenEval addresses C69-C72 regarding motif analysis, while peer review (R5) addresses C69-C72, C87 regarding expression patterns and temporal regulation. Both support the functional role of these elements.

Strong agreement on preimplantation development expression patterns. Both evaluations support claims C73-C83, C138 regarding ZNF789 downregulation, MER21C activation timing, and GPR1-AS expression in human embryos. Reviewers accepted the temporal correlation analysis without critique.

Agreement on conserved epigenomic features despite sequence divergence. Both evaluations support claims C84-C88 regarding ChIP-Atlas analysis and functional conservation. Reviewers affirmed that expression patterns support the role in temporal regulation during development.

Strong agreement on the central evolutionary conclusion. Both evaluations support claims C23, C92, C117-C118, C121 regarding the novel mechanism of retrotransposon-derived LTR involvement in genomic imprinting. Editor and reviewers explicitly confirmed the evidence is convincing and the mechanism is novel.

Agreement on methodological requirements for GPR1-AS detection. Both evaluations address claims C44-C47 regarding RNA-seq depth and quality requirements. Peer review explicitly acknowledges the methodological consideration and validates the approach through generation of new data.

Agreement on the importance of comparative genomics approach. Both evaluations support claims C107, C119-C120 regarding the methodological insight. OpenEval also includes C108 (speculative about future applications). Reviewers explicitly praised the comparative multi-omics approach as critical for identifying MER21C's role.

Minimal overlap on phylogenetic boundary claim C50. OpenEval R8 addresses biallelic expression in non-Euarchontoglire mammals (C50, C55), while peer R10 focuses on comparative methodology (C50, C106-C107, C119-C120). Both support the phylogenetic distribution findings.

OpenEval evaluated background claims C1-C16 regarding established ZDBF2 imprinting knowledge from prior studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual background rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluated background claims C25-C43 regarding established genomic imprinting mechanisms and transposable element roles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these provide conceptual framework from prior literature rather than novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluated contextual claims C90, C93-C95 regarding ZDBF2 function and comparison to other LTR-derived imprinted genes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent background context from prior work.

OpenEval evaluated background claims C109-C116 regarding transposable element regulation and co-option biology. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these describe general biological principles from prior literature rather than novel findings.

OpenEval evaluated claims C97-C103 comparing GPR1-AS to other oocyte-specific LITs and establishing mechanistic distinctions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparative analysis, though the overall conclusions are supported in peer R8.
